item.title: Jameis Winston on losing his starting job: I understand where I am now
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Giants benched Jameis Winston just 23 days after trading with the Vikings for J.J.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants benched Jameis Winston just 23 days after trading with the Vikings for J.J. McCarthy. McCarthy will become the third quarterback to start for the Giants, following Jaxson Dart and Winston.

Dart tore the MCL and meniscus in his left knee in Week 2, ending his season.

Winston started the past four games, going 2-1-1.

He was only 14-of-26 for 152 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions on Sunday, leaving with the Giants trailing 34-10 in the fourth quarter. McCarthy rallied the team, going 11-of-21 for 243 yards, a touchdown and an interception and gave the Giants a chance for a miracle comeback.

That's why Winston accepts returning to a backup role.

"Last game it wasn't what it was capable of being," Winston said, via video from SNY Giants. "Every single week, you're defined off of the last time you stepped foot on the field. So I believe based off last game, my job is to lead the New York Football Giants to a win, and that didn't happen. That being said, I understand where I am now."

Winston has spent most of the past seven seasons as a backup, so he's familiar with the role.

"Just focusing on one day at a time," Winston said. "I'm extremely grateful that I still get to do what I love, and that's play football at a high level for the New York Football Giants. Being able to accept roles and understand like, 'What is your significant role? How can I be the best at my role with this team?' is one of the things you have to adjust to in this league."

item.title: JC Latham on incident with Jordan Elliott: It was just an unfortunate situation
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Titans released defensive lineman Jordan Elliott on Tuesday after an incident at the team facility.
item.content:encoded:
The Titans released defensive lineman Jordan Elliott on Tuesday after an incident at the team facility. An argument with teammate JC Latham last Thursday prompted Elliott to etrieve a gun from his car.

Latham discussed the incident Wednesday.

“It was just an unfortunate situation," Latham said, via Terry McCormick of titaninsider.com. "It was heat of the moment, and shit happens. I don’t really have too much to say about it. . . . There ain’t never been no bad blood between us two. We were here on the summer getting treatment. Before that, we hung out whenever we were in the same city together. We actually had never had an argument leading up to it.

"So I actually think mental health is extremely important, and that’s just one of those situations where you just pray for a guy like that.”

Elliott was dealing with personal issues, per McCormick, when he stormed out of the locker room to the players' garage. Teammate John Franklin-Myers followed Elliott and de-escalated the situation, getting Elliott to put the gun away, McCormick reports.

Latham was grateful to Franklin-Myers.

"I told him I appreciate it," Latham said. "I was still on the field, apparently, . . . so I just told him how much I appreciate him for that."

item.title: The McAfee alt cast underperforms in its debut
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: When ESPN announced that it would produce a Pat McAfee-led alt cast during the Monday night games that don't feature a ManningCast, I sensed trouble on the horizon.
item.content:encoded:
When ESPN announced that it would produce a Pat McAfee-led alt cast during the Monday night games that don't feature a ManningCast, I sensed trouble on the horizon.

The McAfee production, I believed, would consistently outperform the Manning show, creating awkwardness within the Disney family.

A different kind of awkwardness has emerged. The first edition of the McAfee alt cast was outperformed during the same window by a Next Gen Stats alt cast on NFL Network.

Via Austin Karp of Sports Business Journal, the McAfee alt cast on ESPN2 generated 351,000 viewers. The Next Gen Stats edition on NFL Network drew 469,000.

Even with the ManningCast numbers gradually and consistently dropping, it has never dipped to 500,000. At one point, when it was new and fresh (and when the main booth didn't include Joe Buck and Troy Aikman), the ManningCast consistently exceeded one million viewers per game.

As Karp notes, ESPN plans five more McAfee alt casts during the regular season. The next one is set for Bills-Vikings in Week 9. For the Super Bowl, the ManningCast will happen on ESPN2 and the McAfee alt cast will be televised by ESPNU.

Again, unless an alt cast is bringing in people who would otherwise not watch the game, it's a waste of money. The ManningCast has largely been a prestige play, with critics loving it — even if most fans don't want to essentially listen to a podcast while watching a football game. Also, it's a way to get Peyton and Eli on the air together.

McAfee is already ubiquitous for Bristol. The lack of the expected response to a McAfee alt cast could, frankly, be an indication that (after three hours of McAfee on College GameDay and three hours of the Monday of McAfee's show and two hours of McAfee on Monday Night Countdown) his core audience has reached a saturation point by the time the game begins.

item.title: NFL cancels Steelers Fan House event in Paris
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The NFL's approach to Sunday's game in Paris has been to shrug and say, "fi des torpilles."
item.content:encoded:
The NFL's approach to Sunday's game in Paris has been to shrug and say, "fi des torpilles."

Meanwhile, the ongoing unrest has resulted in the cancellation of a Steelers Fan House planned for the days preceding the game.

Via Andrew Fillippoini of 93.7 The Fan in Pittsburgh, the NFL has canceled the event.

"Following recent events in the Bastille neighborhood, and after careful consideration, we felt it appropriate not to move forward with the planned Steelers Fan House event in Paris," the notice posted by Fillipponi explains.

The message reiterates that preparations for the Steelers-Saints game "continue as planned, with the NFL working closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters."

It's fair to ask why the NFL is being so insistent about proceeding with the Paris game in light of the ongoing issues. However small the chance of a problem may be, it's more than zero percent. While the teams will surely have full security at their hotels and at the stadium and during the trips between the two locations, the fans won't be fully secure until they enter the perimeter at the venue.

Meanwhile, any efforts to enhance security at the stadium will necessarily result in fewer resources available to the rest of the city.

While different from the Jalen Hurts situation, there's a common thread. There's a "show must go on" stubbornness that invites unnecessary risk. But with an inflexible top-down directive to proceed, the NFL is proceeding.

Even if the better approach would be to shift the game to London and go back to Paris next year, or whenever it's possible to play the game when the risk of any potential situations is as close to zero as possible.

item.title: Caleb Williams wins NFC offensive player of the week
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Caleb Williams' return was successful, as the quarterback helped pilot the Bears to a 31-23 victory over the Falcons.
item.content:encoded:
Caleb Williams' return was successful, as the quarterback helped pilot the Bears to a 31-23 victory over the Falcons.

Now he’s been named NFC offensive player of the week.

Williams finished 30-of-36 passing for 305 yards with a touchdown and no picks. That performance made him the second QB this season to pass for at least 300 yards on 35 attempts with a completion rate of at least 80 percent.

Geno Smith also accomplished that in Week 3.

This is Williams’ second career offensive player of the week award. He also earned the honor for Week 3 of the 2025 season.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Chiefs will remain without wide receiver Rashee Rice as they kick off the practice week.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs will remain without wide receiver Rashee Rice as they kick off the practice week.

Head coach Andy Reid told reporters that Rice will not practice on Wednesday because of the hamstring injury he suffered in Week 4. The Chiefs had a bye in Week 5 and Rice did not play in last Sunday's win over the Chargers.

Reid said that Rice is improving, but didn't offer any prediction about whether that process will progress fast enough for Rice to make his return against the Seahawks this week.

Right tackle Jaylon Moore will also miss practice after suffering a concussion against the Chargers. Jose Ezeudu replaced him in that game and the Chiefs could get Josh Simmons back into the mix as he continues to work his way back from a back injury.

item.title: Jordan Love dealing with sore back, but expects to play vs. Lions
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Packers quarterback Jordan Love popped up on Wednesday's injury report as limited with a back injury.
item.content:encoded:
Packers quarterback Jordan Love popped up on Wednesday's injury report as limited with a back injury.

But Love told reporters that he's not at risk of missing the Week 7 matchup against Detroit.

“It’s just dealing with a sore back from the game,” Love said, via Bill Huber of SI.com. “Just some lingering effects from that. One of those things, we’ll just take it day by day but, obviously, it was nice to have a jog-through day, a little bit more mental day, and just recover.”

Love was officially hit eight times with three sacks in the Week 6 victory over the Cowboys.

“Obviously, just with the back, I don’t know exactly what play it happened on, when it happened,” Love said. “We talk about all the time: You want to, obviously, limit me taking hits in the pocket. That’s something that we’ve talked about, we harp on, and there’s been some better efforts to do better and protect better. I think guys are responding to that. It’s one of those things, yeah, you want to be able to limit as many hits as I take.”

In his six games this season, Love has completed 60 percent of his throws for 1,684 yards with 11 touchdowns and four interceptions.

item.title: CBS names J.J. Watt its No. 1 analyst beyond 2026
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The upcoming game of broadcaster musical chairs has already begun.
item.content:encoded:
The upcoming game of broadcaster musical chairs has already begun. And one of the seats has already been filled.

CBS announced on Thursday morning that J.J. Watt will serve as the No. 1 NFL analyst beyond his one-year stint as Tony Romo's replacement.

Watt's "multi-year agreement" runs at least through next year's Super Bowl.

“I’ve had a front-row seat to JJ’s growth as a top-tier broadcaster, watching him tackle this role just like he did his hall-of-fame playing career,” Skydance Global Sports Group chairman David Berson said. “He’s insightful, entertaining, passionate, meticulous in his preparation, and the ultimate teammate. He has a unique ability to see things and communicate to fans of all levels. We are thrilled to have him leading our NFL coverage.”

Watt had been the No. 2 analyst at CBS until the network placed Romo on leave in August. CBS and Romo thereafter announced a permanent parting of ways.

The move takes off the table a potential destination for Troy Aikman, Greg Olsen, and others. For Aikman, the only viable spot could be Thursday Night Football. Prime Video has signed Kirk Herbstreit to a bird-in-the-hand extension, but it may not be as cheap to replace him after 2026 as previously reported.

That would leave only the Monday Night Football analyst job, if Aikman and ESPN don't find a way to mend fences. It's possible, frankly, that ESPN already knows who it will hire to replace Aikman. And if that's Greg Olsen, Aikman's only play could be to take the No. 2 spot at Fox — for considerably less than the $30 million annually he reportedly wanted from ESPN. Or the $18 million per year he's currently being paid.

Either way, CBS's decision to keep Watt takes one seat out of play for Aikman, Olsen, Travis Kelce, Sean McVay, or anyone else who may be looking for one of the highest-paying jobs in sports media.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Eagles made changes to the running back room on their 53-man roster on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles made changes to the running back room on their 53-man roster on Tuesday.

They announced that they have signed Elijah Mitchell to their practice squad. They also waived Jaydon Blue and Carson Steele. Steele was waived with an injury designation after hurting his shoulder in Week 6.

Mitchell signed with the Eagles this offseason and returned to the practice squad after being cut in August. He played in one game for the Chiefs last year and ran 327 times for 1,523 yards and nine touchdowns over three seasons with the 49ers.

Blue signed to the active roster ahead of last Sunday's loss to the Panthers, but did not play. Steele had one catch for four yards against Carolina and played in two games overall.

The other backs on the roster are Saquon Barkley and Dameon Pierce. Barkley has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury.

item.title: NFL fines Mike Vrabel, Aaron Glenn, Nick Sirianni $250,000 each for conduct toward officials
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Fines are currently being held in abeyance, and could be repealed.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL isn't messing around when it comes to behavior toward game officials. With an asterisk.

Albert Breer of SI.com reports that the NFL has fined Patriots coach Mike Vrabel, Jets coach Aaron Glenn, and Eagles coach Nick Sirianni $250,000 each for conduct toward game officials.

The discipline may be more performative than substantive. Breer explains that "the fines are in abeyance, meaning they’d be on hold, and could be repealed with good behavior."

It's not entirely clear where things stand, and what it would take to avoid the fines. Also, the amounts are borderline cartoonish. In 2012, former Patriots coach Bill Belichick was fined only $50,000 for confronting and grabbing the arm of a replacement official. Recently, 49ers owner Jed York was fined a mere $500,000 to go along with a six-game suspension after a prostitution-related arrest.

These fines seem over the top, especially since the specific behavior that prompted the fines has not been identified.

In Week 4, Vrabel was flagged for his comments to an official after a disputed call. “I told him it was a terrible — I’m not going to say effing — call,” Vrabel said after the game. “I’ve said that 87 times since I’ve been a head coach. It was nothing derogatory. You’d have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive.”

The league was more than a little sensitive. But it's not as if the $250,000 will be collected. All in all, it feels like an olive branch to the NFL Referees Association, after a pair of suspensions were imposed on officials for interactions with players in Week 5.

item.title: Commanders-49ers attracts 17.9 million viewers for Monday Night Football
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Only 315,000 watched the McAfee alt cast.
item.content:encoded:
Monday night's game between the Commanders and 49ers started as a blowout. The road team eventually turned a 23-3 deficit into a 23-17 nail biter.

The end result, for ratings purposes, resulted in 17.9 million viewers to the various Disney-controlled networks: ABC, ESPN, ESPN2, NFL Network, and ESPN Deportes.

The release from ESPN includes no information regarding the audience to the debut of the Pat McAfee alt cast or the Next Gen Stats broadcast on NFL Network. (Last week, ESPN disclosed that 1.1 million watched the ESPN2 ManningCast and the NFL Network Next Gen Stats presentation, without specifying the audience for either network.)

Andrew Marchand of The Athletic reports that the McAfee alt cast attracted a mere 351,000 viewers, which equates to 1.96 percent of the total audience. That's far less than the ManningCast attracts, even as the Peyton and Eli show continues to slump.

Which brings us back to the overriding question about all alt casts: Why? With the exception of the broadcasts aimed at getting kids to watch by turning the game into a collection of cartoon or video-game characters, there's no reason to siphon viewers from the primary broadcast.

The people who watch the alt casts meant for adults will watch the primary broadcast, in the absence of the alt cast. It's ultimately a pointless exercise that only wastes time and money.

item.title: NFL business partners aren't pulling punches as to the handling of Jalen Hurts
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Eagles' handling of quarterback Jalen Hurts and his blood clot in Week 5 has sparked plenty of criticism of both the team and the league, which has been in lockstep with the team.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles' handling of quarterback Jalen Hurts and his blood clot in Week 5 has sparked plenty of criticism of both the team and the league, which has been in lockstep with the team.

And some of that criticism has come from the NFL's business partners.

The NFL owns 10 percent of ESPN. That hasn't stopped some at ESPN from offering sharp criticism of the league and the Eagles for the situation. On Wednesday's First Take, for instance, Chris "Mad Dog" Russo went off on the situation. (Stephen A. Smith and others had sharp criticism of the situation on Tuesday's show, too.)

"One thing if I may about this whole thing with Hurts, the Eagles did a horrendous job, OK?" Russo said. "And I'm gonna believe the NFL now? That doesn't have grass fields, that didn't do anything with CTE until they were forced to. That wants to play an eighteenth game for the safety of the players, when they want to play another game.

"So the NFL now is saying, 'Well, they didn't do anything wrong. . . . The Eagles were great with this.' I don't trust them. Furthermore, the Eagles throwing Sirianni out there to meet the media. That is ridiculous.  I mean, he doesn't know. I mean, he's not the — put a trainer out there. Put a team doctor. You made the poor guy answer questions with a hungry media in Philadelphia. That was a disgrace.

"And the NFL can't sit there and [say] they care about safety. They care about safety, why are we going for an eighteenth game? They add it to a seventeenth game. Here's the guy that had a blood clot, that got back to the hotel at 3:00 a.m., played the football game, they came back to — flew across the country, came back and said, 'Well, he's gonna miss this week against Carolina.' Then they came back and said, 'He's gonna miss four games.' And then they came back and said, 'He's gone for the year.' That's ridiculous. . . . Now, come on. Literally, come on."

The NFL also has a content partnership with The Athletic, posting items from the New York Times subsidiary at NFL.com. That didn't stop Mike Silver of The Athletic (a former employee of the league who has talked openly about certain subjects being off limits when he worked for NFL Network and NFL.com) from going all-in with his criticism of the Eagles and the league.

"Imagine medically evaluating an employee on an off-site work assignment, subjecting him to well-documented risk factors that could exacerbate the condition — and then having his symptoms worsen to the point where they are potentially life-threatening," Silver wrote in a column posted on Wednesday.

"Then imagine proclaiming to the world that you are in no way culpable, and that any suggestion that you could possibly have handled the situation differently is an affront to logic and decency. Throw in a touch of indignant condescension, and voila: You are the National Football League."

Silver specifically targeted Tuesday's effort by NFL chief medical officer Allen Sills to downplay the situation.

"Now the NFL, whose medical officials were in the loop when Hurts’ initial blood clot was discovered the night before the game, is in full cover-your-ass mode," Silver wrote. "That’s a curious strategy, given the dots that qualified physicians might connect, made worse by the assertion that none of us — even experts in the field — are qualified to question any of it."

The secrecy, disguised as "patient privacy concerns" (despite multiple statements that spell out Hurts's diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis in full detail), has only added to the interest in getting answers.

On Tuesday, Sills insisted that the handling of Hurts was "very conservative, very patient-focused and appropriately guarded in every step."

Devin McCourty, a 13-year NFL veteran, appearing on Wednesday's PFT Live (NBC is a broadcast partner but not a business or content partner with the league), raised an excellent question. Wouldn't a "very conservative, very patient-focused and appropriately guarded" approach to a player who spent most of the prior night in a hospital for diagnosis and evaluation of a blood clot in his leg have resulted in a decision that he should not play a full-contact pro football game hours later?

Seventeen years ago next week, the NFL was forced by Congress to take brain injuries seriously, 15 years after the formation of the decidedly unserious "Mild Traumatic Brain Injury Committee," which delayed the concussion reckoning for as long as it could. The avoidance of the worst-case scenario as to Hurts has prompted the league to attempt to delay a different sort of reckoning regarding the treatment of serious health conditions not involving the brain.

Fortunately, several of the media companies that are in direct business with the league are resisting the effort to avoid answering fair and tough questions about a lingering culture that could have gotten Jalen Hurts killed.

item.title: J.J. McCarthy on feeling more ready to start: Experience does wonders
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: McCarthy will make his first start for the Giants this week.
item.content:encoded:
J.J. McCarthy was drafted 10th overall in 2024 to be the quarterback for the Vikings, but his path to a long run as a starter in the NFL now goes through New Jersey.

McCarthy will make his first start for the Giants in Sunday's game against the Texans and he could have an 11-game run to show the entire league what he's capable of doing. McCarthy said on Wednesday that he sees the move to the first team as "a chance to prove yourself" and that he feels more prepared for the job than he was when he took over as the Vikings' starter at the start of last season.

McCarthy said that he gained knowledge about "the nature of NFL football" in 10 starts between injuries for the Vikings and is confident he'll be able to handle things better despite only being with the Giants for a few weeks.

"I believe just experience does wonders," McCarthy said, via a transcript from the team. "Being able to be in that same situation where you might have made a mistake the last time, this time you're just going to react better and make a more well-rounded response decision in that situation. Just being around great talent and great coaches, absolutely love everyone on the offensive side of the ball and the defensive side of the ball does a tremendous job of just giving us opportunities and always making sure we stay in the game and fight to the last seconds of each game."

Jaxson Dart is still the long-term plan at quarterback for the Giants, but there will be a market for McCarthy if he shows the skills that made him a top pick two years ago and he now has to make the most of his chance to display them.

item.title: A.J. Brown on Sunday's rough outing: I'm moving forward
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Patriots wide receiver A.J.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown had a terrible, horrible, no good, very bad day on Sunday. He caught only four of 10 targets and had three drops in his return to the lineup after four weeks on injured reserve.

With another game on Thursday, Brown had to move on quickly.

“I think that was the hardest part, you know, getting open. I just didn’t make the play,” Brown said Tuesday, via Mark Daniels of Mass Live. “I’m not really going backwards because it’s over with now. You know, I watched the film, I put it to bed, and I’m looking forward.”

Brown was diagnosed with a high ankle sprain in Week 1.

He didn't blame his ankle or rustiness for his poor play and said he won't change anything for this week's game against the Bears.

“No, same process as before,” Brown said. “You know, doing my daily things, getting ready for the game, preparing. Go out here and make plays and leave it at that.”

Patriots quarterback Drake Maye still has faith in his No. 1 wide receiver.

“I mean, it’s A.J. Brown,” Maye said. “Last week is what it is. You know, I wish I had some throws back and, throw some targets his way. And I think it’s part of this league. You want to, you know, make a play so bad. You want to have plays back. There are plays which I want back every week, and that’s part of it.”

item.title: Sauce Gardner says current calf injury isn't as bad as last year
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: A calf injury kept Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner off the field for much of the seven-game losing streak that ended the 2025 season, so his appearance on Wednesday's injury report with another calf injury conjures up some bad memories.
item.content:encoded:
A calf injury kept Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner off the field for much of the seven-game losing streak that ended the 2025 season, so his appearance on Wednesday's injury report with another calf injury conjures up some bad memories.

Gardner was injured early in the second half of last Sunday's loss to the Titans and he missed practice on Wednesday, but he tried to offer some reassurance while speaking to reporters. Gardner said the injury is in a different spot and is "much more minor" than the previous one.

"I'm not really concerned," Gardner said, via the team's website. "I trust our training staff here, and like I said, it's not as bad as last year. I'm just happy that it's not the same spot."

Gardner missed practice a couple of days after General Manager Chris Ballard's firing and moving two first-round picks in a trade for the cornerback has come up often as people recount Ballard's missteps. The deal will only look worse if the Colts wind up at the bottom of the league and that's a more likely outcome if Gardner is forced to the sideline for any significant amount of time.

item.title: Cam Jurgens: Being traded while in concussion protocol is wild, but excited to be a Raven
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Ravens listed Cam Jurgens as a full participant in practice on Wednesday, which suggests that the center will be making his debut for the team when they face the Bengals on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens listed Cam Jurgens as a full participant in practice on Wednesday, which suggests that the center will be making his debut for the team when they face the Bengals on Sunday.

Jurgens was traded to the Ravens a couple of weeks ago, but has missed both of the team's games because of a concussion he suffered at the end of his time with the Eagles. On Wednesday, Jurgens said that acclimating himself to a new team while working through the concussion protocol has been an interesting process that he's looking forward to leaving in the past.

"It's been a wild process," Jurgens said, via the team's website. "Has anybody been traded while they're in the concussion protocol? It just feels so good to be out of this protocol and start to feel a little bit like myself again. I love it here, enjoying it. Anytime you get traded it's such a crazy, whirlwind experience. But this is such a good organization. I'm happy, excited to be here."

Jurgens played guard at the end of his time with the Eagles, but is moving back to center for a Ravens team that's lost three of them to major injuries already this year. Rookie Vega Ioane had moved inside, but he'll return to right guard and the Ravens will hope that the rejiggered line gels quickly in a big game for the AFC North playoff race.

item.title: Jerry Jeudy: Frustrating not to be involved as much, but I just stay focused
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jerry Jeudy spent a lot of time as the top attraction in the Browns' wide receiving corps over the last two years, but his role has changed in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Jerry Jeudy spent a lot of time as the top attraction in the Browns' wide receiving corps over the last two years, but his role has changed in 2026.

Rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston moved to the top of the depth chart and the changing of the guard was illustrated by Jeudy having two catches on five targets through the first three weeks of the season. The last three weeks have seen Jeudy get more involved, including key late catches in wins over the Steelers and Ravens, but he's still playing a complementary rather than a starring role in the offense.

On Wednesday, Jeudy admitted that it's not an ideal situation but that he's still determined to be what quarterback Deshaun Watson and the offense need him to be.

“It’s kind of frustrating not being able to perform or be involved as much as you like, but Deshaun, he just came up to me and he said, ‘Hey, I’m going to need you some of these games, man. I’m going to need you to lock in and stay focused,’" Jeudy said, via Dan Labbe of Cleveland.com. "And I heard that. I just continue to grind and continue to stay focused.”

The change of circumstances has led to speculation that the Browns could move Jeudy ahead of the trade deadline. Jeudy's seen that chatter, but declined to share any conversations he may have had with the Browns about it and said he's "keeping it day-by-day" as the season unfolds in Cleveland.

item.title: Steelers' Yahya Black says he weighs 370 in mic'd up talk with 340-pound Tristan Wirfs
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Buccaneers offensive tackle Tristan Wirfs doesn't often come across people bigger than him, but he did on Sunday, when he played against Steelers defensive tackle Yahya Black.
item.content:encoded:
Buccaneers offensive tackle Tristan Wirfs doesn't often come across people bigger than him, but he did on Sunday, when he played against Steelers defensive tackle Yahya Black.

Wirfs was mic’d up for NFL Films, which revealed an on-field conversation with Black about their respective sizes. The discussion went like this:

Black: "What they got you weighing at?"

Wirfs: "340. What about you?"

Black: "370"

Wirfs: "I knew it. You look huge."

Black: "Thank you. I try."

Wirfs: "No, I mean, you look great. You look like an absolute unit."

Wirfs and Black both played at Iowa, though not together. Wirfs' third and final year at Iowa was 2019, when he was a first-team All-American and won the Big Ten's lineman of the year award. Black's first year at Iowa was 2020, and Wirfs told teammates in the Buccaneers' huddle on Sunday that he visited Iowa after his rookie season in the NFL and met a younger and much smaller Black.

"When I went back to train after my rookie year, he was a freshman. He was not that big," Wirfs said in the Bucs' huddle. "He's, like, doubled in size."

Later, Wirfs complimented Black on his apparel when he attended a recent Iowa game as a spectator, and wondered where men their size can get clothes that fit.

Wirfs: "Where did you get your overalls for the Iowa game?"

Black: "Bro, I just walked into a shop downtown."

Wirfs: "No way!"

Black: "4X, baby."

Both Wirfs and Black have gained weight while in the league. Wirfs weighed in at 320 pounds at the 2020 Scouting Combine. Black weighed 336 at the 2025 Scouting Combine.

item.title: Roger Goodell on Jed York suspension: "We saw a violation and we dealt with it"
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: 49ers owner Jed York attended the league meeting this week upon the conclusion of his six-game suspension.
item.content:encoded:
49ers owner Jed York attended the league meeting this week upon the conclusion of his six-game suspension. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell defended that suspension as an appropriate consequence of York violating the same personal conduct policy that applies to players and everyone else in the league.

York pleaded no contest to two misdemeanors after he was arrested in a prostitution sting in East Palestine, Ohio. Goodell said at the league meeting that the personal conduct policy "applies to owners, commissioners, everybody else, players." That's true, but the $500,000 fine York paid is a pittance compared to what players can lose if they receive a comparable suspension. A player who is suspended six games loses one-third of his salary for that season; $500,000 is nothing remotely close to one-third of what York or any other owner makes in a season.

"We went through a full process, obviously, to understand the facts, understand the issues. Looked at it under the context of our personal conduct policy," Goodell said.

Goodell said the league stands by its personal conduct policy and that the discipline York faced was appropriate for the violation he committed.

"It's something we feel strongly about," Goodell said. "We think we need to represent ourselves and our organizations properly. We saw a violation and we dealt with it from a discipline standpoint. That concluded now, so he'll be back representing the 49ers."

item.title: Dolphins are raising all season ticket prices for 2027
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: For the 0-5 Dolphins, who have yet to take the lead in any game this season, the phrase "better luck next year" already applies.
item.content:encoded:
For the 0-5 Dolphins, who have yet to take the lead in any game this season, the phrase "better luck next year" already applies. So does the phrase "better get ready to pay more money next year."

Via Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald, the Dolphins will be raising season ticket prices "across the board in 2027."

The team attributes the increase to hosting nine regular-season games next season. In 2026, the team increased prices for none of the season tickets — and dropped the prices for some of them.

Per Jackson, most tickets will increase by three percent. Some of them (specifically, in the shade on the home sideline) will be bumped a "bit more."

In two home games played so far this year, the Dolphins have averaged 58,719 attendees. That ranks 31st in the league, ahead of only the Jaguars — whose ongoing renovations have reduced capacity to 42,000 for 2026.

Last year, the Dolphins averaged 65,687 in eight home games, with the ninth played in Spain.

item.title: Matthew Stafford hopes fans see injuries for more than just the impact on fantasy teams
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "Everybody sees these and they're on their fantasy team or whatever," Stafford said. "We're like, 'That guy's worked his ass off for eight months to get this opportunity.'"
item.content:encoded:
Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford wants fans to understand what player injuries really mean.

Stafford said he personally felt the impact from learning Rams receiver Davante Adams will miss most of the rest of the season, and it means a lot more than just his impact on fantasy football teams.

"Like Davante, disappointed for those guys," Stafford said. "Everybody sees these and they're on their fantasy team or whatever, and they're like, 'I gotta trade a guy in and out now.' And we're like, 'That guy's worked his ass off for eight months to get this opportunity and it's unfortunate he doesn't get to do what he loves to do.' So I feel more for our guys than I do for anybody else, and I know the work that they put into it, to be out here doing what they love. So that hurts me for them."

Stafford said one of the things motivating him to play hard in the weeks ahead is wanting the Rams to still be in playoff contention when Adams, Myles Garrett and other injured teammates return.

"I feel even more a responsibility to be as good as I can to be help us continue to win," Stafford said. "Some of those guys, they're gonna have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us it's meaningful."

Stafford said he hopes people realize the true impact of injuries is on players like Adam, who desperately want to be able to play and currently can't.

"Disappointed for him," Stafford said. "I know how hard he works to be out there for us, and when he's not able to do that it tears him up."

item.title: In their SoFi Stadium incident, Troy Aikman's position to Joe Buck was: "You f—ked me over!"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: New report adds details to the tension in the MNF booth.
item.content:encoded:
The 25-year partnership between Joe Buck and Troy Aikman is moving toward a conclusion, and more details have emerged regarding last week's tipping point at SoFi Stadium.

Dylan Byers of Puck adds some color to the prior report of tension between the Monday Night Football broadcaster team.

“There had been weeks of Troy becoming increasingly cold, difficult, short, making comments,” a source with direct knowledge of the situation told Byers. “Joe finally snapped,” the source told Byers, in reference to the Week 5 incident at the Bills-Rams game. “He basically said, 'Dude, are we really going to do this?' And Troy’s position was: You fucked me over!”

Said another unnamed source to Byers, “They exchanged some very direct and honest feelings."

Byers, who says he spoke to more than a dozen sources, writes that Aikman "felt like a lot of people had fucked him over."

It came down to Buck cutting a deal on his extension, with the understanding that he may have a new partner in 2027. But Aikman also had been trying to do his own deal; per Byers, one of Aikman's agents pegged his value at $30 million per year — a sizable jump over his current rate of $18 million.

Aikman "saw it as the ultimate act of betrayal,” an unnamed source told Byers. “They cut this deal in May and put it in a drawer. ESPN didn’t tell him, Joe didn’t tell him.”

Ultimately, it's everyone for themselves. Aikman asked for too much. Buck made a more realistic demand. If it had been the other way around, Aikman would have his deal and Buck would be waiting for an offer that, at this point, may never come.

Byers reports that, on the most recent Monday night in Santa Clara, Buck apologized to Aikman and the entire production team for losing his cool. Buck's message was, per Byers, "We’re all adults, we’ve all got jobs to do, let’s move forward, let’s have a great year.” Aikman reportedly added nothing after Buck said what he had to say.

The whole thing is odd, to say the least, if not unprecedented. At this point, it seems like Aikman will be leaving, likely for CBS or Prime Video. And Buck, armed with his new contract, will be sticking around.

Through it all, they'll be working together for the rest of a season that culminates in ESPN's first Super Bowl.

At a time when ESPN is trying its best to relentlessly hype the February 14 event, the Aikman-Buck situation becomes a potential distraction. Or maybe it adds a little extra sizzle, given the possibility that their tenuous relationship could lead to an on-air incident at some point between now and the final game of the 2026 season.

item.title: UFL has a stadium issue in St. Louis for 2027
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: St.
item.content:encoded:
St. Louis has been one of the UFL's success stories, with fans packing the stadium where the Rams previously played. But there's a problem for 2027, as explained by UFL co-owner Mike Repole in a lengthy post on Twitter.

As Repole puts it, the available dates at their home stadium mean that the BattleHawks "would play FOUR straight home games, followed by FIVE consecutive road games, and potentially return home for Week 10."

"FOUR HOME GAMES. FIVE ROAD GAMES. Sorry, but that just DOESN’T WORK FOR US!!!!" Repole said.

Repole added that it doesn't mean the UFL is leaving St. Louis. Really, why would they go? They have a strong following there.

He didn't identify the scheduling conflicts, and it's odd that the local authorities would load up the weekends in which it knew, or should have known, that the UFL would be playing.

Regardless, Repole has opted to take the issue public. Whether that changes things remains to be seen.

item.title: After two years rehabbing, Tank Dell overwhelmed, anxious and excited to play again
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Texans wide receiver Tank Dell has not played a game since Dec. 21, 2024, when he tore multiple ligaments and dislocated his kneecap in a game against the Chiefs.
item.content:encoded:
Texans wide receiver Tank Dell has not played a game since Dec. 21, 2024, when he tore multiple ligaments and dislocated his kneecap in a game against the Chiefs. The gruesome knee injury threatened his career.

"I’m blessed," Dell said, via DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN. "I want to thank God for getting me back in this position. But I don't think I'm overwhelmed. I'm anxious, of course, but I don't think I'm overwhelmed. I'm anxious to get back out there and play some football."

The Texans opened Dell's practice window on Oct. 5, and he returns to game action on Sunday against the Giants.

"I know it's a lot of questions, like, 'How he gonna look when he gets tackled?'" Dell said. "I don't care about none of that. I'm ready to get tackled. I'm gonna be joyful. Y'all gonna see the passion I have after I had that first catch."

Dell, a third-round pick in 2023, will likely be on a snap count Sunday. That doesn't matter to him or to the Texans.

"It's just getting Tank back out there after missing two years of football," Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said. "That's the main thing. Him just going out playing ball. I don't care how many reps he gets. But I'll have my Tank Dell jersey on."

Dell has 98 receptions for 1,376 yards and 10 touchdowns in his career.

item.title: NFL could embrace replay review transparency by the end of the current season
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Transparency apparently is coming, thanks to the UFL, the ACC, and the Big Ten.
item.content:encoded:
In July, Broncos coach Sean Payton predicted that the NFL will adopt UFL-style officiating transparency within the next two to three years.

It could be coming sooner than that.

A Wednesday item from Albert Breer of SI.com includes this nugget: "[P]lanning is underway for more transparency. I’m told the NFL has watched closely at how the ACC and, after the Michigan–Western Michigan debacle, the Big Ten have started televising their replay review process. The idea of doing something similar to show the public replay reviews is being discussed, and work is being done to implement something similar to what we’ve seen in college football very soon, potentially in the coming weeks, and certainly (some in the league office hope) before the end of the regular season."

It would be stunning if it happens during the current season. The NFL rarely makes significant change while a season is unfolding.

Regardless, it's better sooner than later, and later than never. The NFL needs to follow the lead of the UFL, the ACC, and the Big Ten. It's the NFL that's supposed to be the leader when it comes to football innovation. It's already behind the times, and the lack of transparency fuels conspiracy theories.

If the league does it, the question becomes whether the league can do it properly. The only thing worse than no transparency would be transparency into a flawed process.

So, yes, be careful what you wish for. Seeing the sausage get made could potentially cause you to swear off eating it.

item.title: Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love remains out of practice
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love is improving, Mike LaFleur said.
item.content:encoded:
Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love is improving, Mike LaFleur said.

Love, though, did not practice Wednesday.

Love has not practiced since Oct. 9 due to a lingering ankle injury. He injured the ankle in Week 4, played 36 of 73 snaps in Week 5 and missed the Week 6 win over the Rams on Sunday.

The Cardinals also practiced without safety Budda Baker (groin/illness), defensive lineman Walter Nolen III (ankle), offensive lineman Isaac Seumalo (rest), outside linebacker Josh Sweat (rest), cornerback Garrett Williams (knee), offensive lineman Jedrick Wills Jr. (illness) and safety Andrew Wingard (knee).

Rookie quarterback Carson Beck (back), cornerback Max Melton (knee) and safety Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) were limited.
